question.problem: Let $X$ and $Y$ be discrete random variables, and suppose $\text{E}[X∣Y]=5Y-4.$ If $\text{E}[X]=11,$ what is $\text{E}[Y]?$
question.worked_solution:
We are given an expression for $\text{E}[X∣Y]$ in terms of $Y,$ and the value of $\text{E}[X].$ This is a direct application of the tower property, which states that

$$
\text{E}[X]=\text{E}[\text{E}[X∣Y]].
$$

So, we substitute the given expression for the inner expectation, which gives

$$
\text{E}[X]=\text{E}[5Y-4].
$$

Now, we apply the linearity of expectation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =\text{E}[5Y-4] \\  & =5\cdot \text{E}[Y]-4\end{aligned}
$$

We are told that $\text{E}[X]=11,$ so we solve this equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}11 & =5\cdot \text{E}[Y]-4 \\ 15 & =5\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\ \text{E}[Y] & =3\end{aligned}
$$
